done_when: forge read records a round as passed when its only numbered items say there are no findings (in any common wording), and notes like 'tests were not run' don't count as findings; the reader's instructions ask for the plain no-findings form; a real finding still fails the round; a command test with a faked reader covers the numbered 'No findings' form, the plain form and a real finding, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: The previous `detected` and test-note examples are repaired, but new unambiguous counterexamples remain: `6. There are no findings.`, `6. No bugs found.`, and `6. No findings reported.` Each fails this recognizer because its prefix, noun, or suffix is excluded. Consequently, the record-writing code at `src/forge/story.py:276` writes `passed: no`, recreating the unnecessary disposition and read round. These replies contain no substantive finding and fall within the promised “any common wording”; they do not require accepting arbitrary explanations contrary to the coordinator’s ruling. Extend recognition conservatively and cover these cases in the existing command table for both client histories.
findings.title: Not done: forge read still rejects common no-findings wording

why: A cold read that found nothing is recorded as not passed when the reader writes 'No findings' as a numbered item (for example '6. No findings.' plus a note that tests weren't run), so forge next asks for a disposition on it and the plan pays an extra read round (reported by a client session, 2026-10-09)
